description: Fast and lightweight DB Client made in Rust and GPUI.
name: dbdelve
readme_text: # DBDelve A fast, native, cross-platform, multi-engine database client. Written in Rust with GPUI, no Electron and no JVM: instant startup, friendly on your memory, and smooth scrolling through large tables where other clients crash or introduce limits. ## Community Ideas and discussion on [Discord](https://discord.gg/7PegWzwqCm). Like DBDelve? [Support its development](https://www.patreon.com/cw/ShayanAbbas1). Support is voluntary and does not provide any additional benefits. ![DBDelve in Gruvbox Dark Glass: a SELECT on the events table in the editor and its result grid below](assets/screenshots/query-dark.png) ![DBDelve in Gruvbox Light Glass: a join in the editor and its result grid below](assets/screenshots/query-light.png) Scrolling a million rows: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e15d566-a110-46c6-a236-52af7d877d4c Launching, with the last results already there: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e55da56-8577-43e0-812a-c77eb5d0e701 ## Why I wanted something which is performant, modern and consumes little ram. The existing DB clients are either filled with bloat (Electron and JVM) or paid. This is an alternative to them. No feature is ever going behind a paywall and with time we will have complete parity on features with those too. ## Install **macOS** (Apple Silicon, macOS 12 or later): ```sh brew install --cask ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/dbdelve xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/DBDelve.app ``` Don't skip the second line: the app isn't notarized, so macOS won't open it until the quarantine flag is cleared. **Linux** (x86_64 or aarch64): `yay -S dbdelve-bin` from the AUR, or the tarball or AppImage from [the latest release][releases]. **Windows** (x86_64): run the installer from [the latest release][releases], or unzip the zip and run `dbdelve.exe`. The installer asks for AppData (just for you) or Program Files (all users). Updating, the `.dmg`, Linux requirements, building from source and where your data lives are all in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md). [releases]: https://github.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/releases/latest ## Supported databases Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Turso, DuckDB, Snowflake, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis (and Valkey, KeyDB, Dragonfly) and ClickHouse. Any other database with an ODBC driver is reachable through the bundled ODBC bridge, with that driver installed: IBM Db2, Oracle, SAP HANA, SAP ASE (Sybase), Informix, Teradata, Vertica, Exasol, Firebird, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, Databricks, Apache Hive, Trino and Presto, Dremio, InterSystems IRIS, Microsoft Access and more. Grid editing is off, and statements you type run under the connection's mode. See [Connecting through ODBC](docs/odbc.md). ![The welcome screen: paste a connection URL or pick one of the engines, import from DBeaver or TablePlus, or pick a theme](assets/screenshots/welcome.png) ## What it does - **Make it yours.** The app's own themes alongside Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Gruvbox and Dracula, each in dark, light and glass. Import themes from Zed or VS Code, or [write your own](docs/themes.md). ![The theme picker, with themes imported from Zed and VS Code and the import commands below them](assets/screenshots/themes.png) - **Bring your connections with you.** Import every saved connection, passwords and SSH settings included, from DBeaver, or TablePlus on macOS. - **Organize your connections into projects,** and jump to any of them from the palette, or disconnect back to a home screen that lists them all. ![The palette scoped to connections, grouped into two projects, with the current connection marked](assets/screenshots/projects.png) - **Never mistake prod for staging.** Every connection is isolated and can color the title bar. Run it read-only, read-write or with full access, and DBDelve asks before anything destructive. ![The connection form, grouped into connection, security and behaviour, with a color and a project for the connection](assets/screenshots/connection-form.png) - **Edits you can read first.** Change a cell and DBDelve writes the `UPDATE` for you to check before it runs. - **Keep the columns you need.** Hide or pin columns, and the layout survives a restart. - **Read a row in full** in the row panel, with JSON highlighted, and edit long values there. ![A table open in the grid, with the row panel showing one row's values and its JSON highlighted](assets/screenshots/table-dark.png) - **Import rows** from CSV, TSV or JSON, with every row checked and every statement shown before anything runs. ![Importing events.csv: format options on the left, each file column mapped to a table column, and a preview of the rows](assets/screenshots/import.png) - **Open a data file** by dropping it on the window: a CSV, Excel, Parquet or JSON file opens in DuckDB, held in memory, as a query you can change. A `.sql` file opens in a new query tab on the connection you're on, and runs only when you run it. - **See the query plan** highlighted in its own pane, with bad row estimates called out. ![An Explain Analyze plan for a join: each node with its actual and estimated rows and time, and a ×76 misestimate flagged](assets/screenshots/query-plan.png) - **Completion that knows your schema:** tables, and a table's columns after its name and a dot. ![Completing accounts. to its columns in a join](assets/screenshots/completion.png) - **Keyboard-first.** One palette for commands, tables, saved queries, history and connections, and every shortcut rebindable. - **Your SSH, not a reimplementation.** Tunnels run through your own `ssh`, so your config, agent and hardware keys just work. For Postgres, a Host that is a directory (`/var/run/postgresql`) reaches that Unix socket on the SSH host, optionally as another user (Run as); the server needs `socat`, and passwordless `sudo` for it when Run as is set. TLS modes other than `disable` and `prefer` are refused there. Free and open source, nothing behind a paywall, and no telemetry: the only request DBDelve makes on its own is an update check, which you can turn off. ## Benchmarks DBDelve 0.3.6 against DBeaver 25.3.1 on the same Postgres table, median of 5 runs each (2026-10-11, M1 Pro, 32 GB): | | DBDelve | DBeaver | | ----------------- | ------- | ------- | | Launch | 1.1 s | 5.2 s | | Idle memory | 133 MB | 606 MB | | 1,000-row query | 0.21 s | 1.96 s | | 1M rows, time | 56 s | 208 s | | 1M rows, memory\* | 4.9 GB | 17 GB | \* The whole 1M-row table pulled into memory on purpose, with the row limit off. Method and full results in [BENCHMARKS.md](BENCHMARKS.md). ## Logs and bug reports DBDelve keeps a diagnostic log on your machine and never sends it anywhere. To attach it to an issue, use **Help → Copy Diagnostics** and paste; **Help → Open Logs Folder** shows the files. If the default log doesn't show the problem, turn on **Verbose logging** in Settings and reproduce it. Read a log before you post it and remove anything sensitive. A verbose one can hold hostnames, database names and anything a database driver logs. ## License Copyright (C) 2026 Shayan Abbas and contributors, licensed under the [GPL-3.0](LICENSE). Code contributed before the switch was released under the [MIT License](licenses/MIT-dbdelve.txt), and that notice still applies to it.
